thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: inferpool-usw2 (inference-pool) - multiple nodes NotReady (kubelet restarts). Severity: SEV2. PD alert id: PD-82431
Samira Khan: seeing it, oncall responding. starting quick triage.
Samira Khan: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-usw2 -o wide` shows 6/24 nodes NotReady, kubelet restarts 3-5x in last 10m.
Jason Lee: any recent deploys or kernel/driver churn?
Samira Khan: no deploys in the last hour, infra autoscaler activity around 02:03 but that looks normal. GPU driver logs show repeated: `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` on affected nodes.
Kevin Ortiz: that smells like a driver/kernel race + hw flappy. can we cordon the flapping nodes and failover traffic?
Maya Chen: customer telemetry: a subset of hosted customers hitting increased 502/503 for short bursts, and latency p95 doubled for streaming endpoints routed to usw2. Escalating product impact.
Samira Khan: cordoning flappers now and kicking pods to fallback pool. `/scripts/ops cordon-node ip-10-0-23-45 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-23-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
infra-bot: Drain jobs started for 6 nodes. Estimated pod moves: ~120.
Jason Lee: starting routing policy change: steer inference requests away from usw2 to usw1 and eu-west as fallback. Updating smart-router policy to prefer region bias -20 for usw2.
Samira Khan: pushed routing bias, confirm traffic shift in progress.
Kevin Ortiz: meanwhile I'll try to repro on one affected node: collecting dmesg + kubelet logs. attaching snippet:```kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:01:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus```
Samira Khan: heap of OOM/CUDA complaints too: container logs show `cudaMalloc() failed: out of memory` and then `kubelet: container runtime error: container crashed` intermittently.
Maya Chen: customer impact note: two self-serve customers (acct: acme-corp, acct: lilt-ai) reported errors between 02:05-02:12. support already sent status update.
Jason Lee: action items: 1) cordon+drain flappers (in progress) 2) reroute traffic (done) 3) spin up additional fallback capacity in usw1 (requested) 4) capture node-level logs and disable problematic kernel module if repro.
Samira Khan: handoff to infra: tagging @Kevin and @Jason to continue remediation. I'm going offline for a quick break, keeping Slack notifications on. ETA ~20m.
Kevin Ortiz: got a node repro. looks like GPU driver 525.89 with kernel 5.15 timing issue. temporary mitigation: blacklist nvidia-uvm on affected nodes and restart kubelet? thinking safer: drain and reprovision node with driver roll-back.
infra-bot: reprovision job queued: reprovision-image: inference-gpu-ubuntu-20.04:v3 -> will apply to drained nodes. Estimated time per node: ~6m.
Jason Lee: started spin-up of dedicated fallback pool (dedicated-small) to absorb steady traffic, autoscaler bumped replicas.
Maya Chen: posting interim customer status: "We are seeing increased errors in US-West2 due to node instability. Traffic is being routed to other regions; mitigation in progress. No data loss. Engineers are working on repro and reprovisioning."
Samira Khan: thanks. hooking incident ticket PD-82431 -> INC-2026-072 for postmortem.
Kevin Ortiz: reprovision completed for 4 nodes, kernels/drivers pinned to stable combo. Remaining 2 nodes reprovisioning now.
Jason Lee: router reports 92% of traffic moved off usw2. error rates dropping. latency returning to baseline on routed requests.
infra-bot: all drained nodes reprovisioned and returned to Ready state. kubelet restarts count back to normal.
Maya Chen: verifying customer signals: support confirms acme-corp saw retry success and lilt-ai back to normal. no broader customer escalations.
Samira Khan: signing back in, thanks team. I'm going to follow up with a short postmortem template and schedule a blameless review with infra/serving teams.
Jason Lee: marking incident as mitigated in PD. I'll own the follow-up: check driver rollout gating and add node-level telemetry to catch NVRM early.
Kevin Ortiz: note for postmortem: consider temporary autoscaler policy to avoid scaling into nodes with older driver images during rollout windows.
Maya Chen: will close customer-facing update once PD marked mitigated.
Samira Khan: ok closing thread for now, re-open if we see re-appearance. :thumbsup:
